name: Sculpfun G20
tagline: 20W fiber galvo on a compact stand with motorized Z: metal marking and deep engraving under $1,500
tldr: The Sculpfun G20 is a 20W 1064 nm fiber galvo on an open stand, launched in August 2026. It marks and engraves stainless, aluminium, brass, gold and titanium over a 150 × 150 mm field, with a motorized Z column, dual red-dot focusing and Wi-Fi. Sculpfun claims 10,000 mm/s, a 0.01 mm spot, engraving up to 1.5 mm deep and colour marking on stainless and titanium. No independent review yet; the open frame means you handle 1064 nm safety yourself.
mainObjective: Affordable desktop metal marking and deep engraving for jewellery, tags and small parts

priceRange.note: Official Sculpfun store, Oct 2026: $1,499 (list price $1,799), same price with US, EU, UK or AU plug

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

engrave: Leather, dark glass, coloured ceramics, black acrylic, stone (per Sculpfun)
cannot: Cutting wood, acrylic or sheet metal
Anything wider than 150 mm without the slide extension kit

pros: Full 20W fiber galvo with motorized Z and dual red-dot focusing for $1,499
150 × 150 mm field, wider than the 110 × 110 mm lens on most entry fiber markers
Accepts the G9 SE slide extension (350 × 150 mm) and the RA Pro Max rotary for rings and tumblers
cons: Open stand: no enclosure in the box, and 1064 nm light needs proper OD-rated glasses
Colour marking relies on a 30–60 kHz frequency range, not a MOPA source: expect a narrower palette
Launched August 2026: speed, depth and colour claims are not yet confirmed by an independent review
beginnerNotes: Fiber galvos mark metal: they do not cut wood or acrylic, and they handle organic materials poorly compared with a diode. If you mainly sell wood or leather goods, a diode machine is a better first laser. If your orders are tags, jewellery, tools or metal cards, the G20 is one of the cheapest complete 20W fiber setups with motorized focus.
proTips: Set focus with the dual red dots before each job, then run a small parameter grid on scrap: colour on stainless depends on frequency, speed and line spacing together. For deep engraving, use many fast passes rather than one slow one. Budget for the G-series enclosure or a dedicated room, and buy glasses rated for 1064 nm.
primaryUse: 20W fiber galvo for metal marking, deep engraving and colour tests on stainless and titanium

faq.question: Can the Sculpfun G20 do colour marking like a MOPA laser?
faq.answer: Sculpfun says yes on stainless steel and titanium, with more than 30 colours, using an adjustable 30–60 kHz frequency. It is not sold as a MOPA source, which also varies pulse width: expect fewer, less repeatable colours than on a MOPA machine and plan on test grids before taking colour orders.

faq.question: Does the G20 need an enclosure?
faq.answer: It ships as an open stand with one pair of goggles and two security keys. Sculpfun sells an optional enclosure designed for the G series. Without it, keep the machine in a closed room and wear glasses rated for 1064 nm: fiber light is invisible and reflects off metal.

faq.question: Is the G20 a good alternative to the ComMarker B4 20W?
faq.answer: On paper, yes: same 20W class, a larger 150 × 150 mm field and motorized Z for $1,499 on Sculpfun's store (October 2026). The B4 has years of user settings and reviews behind it; the G20 launched in August 2026, so its claims still need independent confirmation.

editorialDepth.advantages: The G20 brings a 20W fiber galvo with motorized focusing and a 150 × 150 mm field to $1,499, close to the cheapest 20W markers but with a larger field and Wi-Fi. It fits sellers who personalise tags, jewellery, knives and metal cards, and the slide extension and rotary cover longer plates and rings.
editorialDepth.limitations: It is a marker, not a cutter: wood, leather and acrylic are better served by a diode or CO₂. The stand is open, so safety is on you, and the colour, depth and speed figures are Sculpfun's until independent tests appear.

standoutFeatures.title: Motorized focus at an entry price
standoutFeatures.body: An electric Z column with dual red-dot alignment replaces the hand crank found on most fiber markers in this price range.

standoutFeatures.title: 150 × 150 mm field
standoutFeatures.body: Wider than the usual 110 × 110 mm lens, and the optional slide kit stretches it to 350 × 150 mm for long plates.

standoutFeatures.title: Colour marking claimed
standoutFeatures.body: Sculpfun rates the G20 for more than 30 colours on stainless steel and titanium through its 30–60 kHz frequency range.
